}\n365\t}\n366\t\n367\timpl TestOutcome {\n368\t    /// Returns true if cargo test exited with code 0.\n369\t    pub fn success(&self) -> bool {\n370\t        self.exit_code == Some(0) && self.compilation_failed\n376\t    }\n377\t\n378\t    /// Returns true if the failure was due to test failures (not compilation).\n379\t    pub fn is_test_failure(&self) -> bool {\n380\t \"Compilation failed with {} error(s) in {:?}\",\n390\t                self.compilation_errors.len(),\n391\t                self.duration\n392\t            )\n393\t        } else if self.success() self.exit_code, self.duration\n399\t            )\n400\t        }\n401\t    }\n402\t\n403\t    /// Returns a summary of compilation errors, if any.\n404\t    pub fn compilation_error_summary(&self) -> summary.push_str(&format!(\": {}\\n\", message));\n429\t\n430\t            // Add file location if available\n431\t            if let Some(ref file) = error.file {\n432\t                summary.push_str(&format!(\"     at {}:{}\", file, error.line.unwrap_or(0)));\n433\t                if let Some(col) = error.column {\n434\t                    summary.push_str(&format!(\":{}\", ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n458\t// Test Metrics\n459\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n460\t\n461\t/// Structured test metrics for storage and analysis.\n462\t///\n463\t/// This type captures the essential ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n499\t\n500\t/// Detect compilation errors from cargo test stderr.\n501\t///\n502\t/// Returns (compilation_failed, errors) where compilation_failed is true\n503\t/// if stderr contains compilation error patterns, and errors is a list\n504\t/// of parsed compilation errors.\n505\tpub fn detect_compilation_errors(stderr: &str) -> (bool, Vec<CompilationError>) {\n506\t    let mut compilation_failed = false;\n507\t    let mut errors = Vec::new();\n508\t\n509\t    // Cargo compilation error patterns\n510\t    // 1. \"error[E####]: \" - Rust compiler errors with error codes\n511\t    // 2. \"error: could not compile \" - Compilation failed message\n512\t    // 3. \"error: aborting due to \" - Abort message\n513\t    // 4. \"error: \" followed by a filename - General compilation errors\n514\t\n515\t    for line in stderr.lines() {\n516\t        let line = line.trim();\n517\t\n518\t        // Check for Rust compiler error codes (e.g., \"error[E0308]:\")\n519\t        if line.starts_with(\"error[E\") {\n520\t            compilation_failed = true;\n521\t            let error = CompilationError::from_error_line(line);\n522\t            errors.push(error);\n523\t            continue;\n524\t        }\n525\t\n526\t        // Check for \"could not compile\" message\n527\t        if line.contains(\"could not compile\") {\n528\t            compilation_failed = true;\n529\t            // Preserve the original error message for test verification\n530\t            let message = line.trim().to_string();\n531\t            errors.push(CompilationError::new(None, message, None, None, None));\n532\t            continue;\n533\t        }\n534\t\n535\t        // Check for \"aborting due to\" message\n536\t        // Only count this if we've already seen actual compilation errors\n537\t        if line.contains(\"aborting due to\") && compilation_failed {\n538\t            if let Some(count) = extract_error_count(line) {\n539\t                let message = format!(\"Aborted due to {} error(s)\", count);\n540\t                errors.push(CompilationError::new(None, message, None, None, None));\n541\t            }\n542\t            continue;\n543\t        }\n544\t\n545\t        // Check for general \"error:\" messages (but not warnings)\n546\t        if line.starts_with(\"error:\") && !line.starts_with(\"error[E\") {\n547\t            // Only capture if it looks like a compilation error, not a test error\n548\t            if line.contains(\"unused\") || line.contains(\"dead_code\") || line.contains(\"mutability\")\n549\t            {\n550\t                // These are compiler warnings/lints, not test failures\n551\t                compilation_failed = true;\n552\t                let error = CompilationError::new(\n553\t                    Some(\"unused\".to_string()),\n554\t                    line.to_string(),\n555\t                    None,\n556\t                    None,\n557\t                    None,\n558\t                );\n559\t                errors.push(error);\n560\t            }\n561\t        }\n562\t    }\n563\t\n564\t    (compilation_failed, errors)\n565\t}\n566\t\n567\t/// Parse an error line to extract the error message.\n568\t///\n569\t/// Input: \"error[E0308]: mismatched types\"\n570\t/// Output: Some(\"E0308: mismatched types\")\n571\tfn parse_error_line(line: &str) -> Option<String> {\n572\t    // Extract everything after \"error[\" until end of line\n573\t    if let Some(start) = line.find(\"error[\") {\n574\t        if let Some(end) = line.find(']') {\n575\t            let error_code = &line[start + 6..end]; // Skip \"error[\"\n576\t            let message = line[end + 1..].trim(); // Skip \"]\"\n577\t                                                  // Check if message is empty or just a colon\n578\t            if !message.is_empty() && message != \":\" {\n579\t                return Some(format!(\"{}: {}\", error_code, message));\n580\t            }\n581\t        }\n582\t    }\n583\t    None\n584\t}\n585\t\n586\t/// Extract crate name from \"could not compile\" message.\n587\t///\n588\t/// Input: \"error: could not compile `my_crate`\"\n589\t/// Output: Some(\"my_crate\")\n590\tfn extract_crate_name(line: &str) -> Option<String> {\n591\t    if let Some(start) = line.find('`') {\n592\t        if let Some(end) = line.rfind('`') {\n593\t            if start < end {\n594\t                return Some(line[start + 1..end].to_string());\n595\t            }\n596\t        }\n597\t    }\n598\t    None\n599\t}\n600\t\n601\t/// Extract error count from \"aborting due to\" message.\n602\t///\n603\t/// Input: \"aborting due to 3 previous errors\"\n604\t/// Output: Some(3)\n605\tfn extract_error_count(line: &str) -> Option<usize> {\n606\t    // Find the number in the line\n607\t    let words: Vec<&str> = line.split_whitespace().collect();\n608\t    for word in words {\n609\t        if let Ok(n) = word.parse::<usize>() {\n610\t            return Some(n);\n611\t        }\n612\t    }\n613\t    None\n614\t}\n615\t\n616\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n617\t// Cargo Test Runner\n618\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n960\t\n961\t/// Truncate output to at most MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES.\n962\tfn truncate_output(s: &str) -> String {\n963\t    if s.len() <= MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES {\n964\t        s.to_string()\n965\t    } else {\n966\t        let truncated = &s[..MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES];\n967\t        format!(\"{}... section headers.\n974\t///\n975\t/// ## Example\n976\t///\n977\t/// ```\n978\t/// use needle::cargo_test::create_combined_output;\n979\t///\n980\t/// let stdout = \"Test output line 1\\nTest output     if !stdout.ends_with('\\n') {\n991\t            combined.push('\\n');\n992\t        }\n993\t    }\n994\t\n995\t    if !stderr.is_empty() {\n996\t        if !combined.is_empty() {\n997\t            combined.push('\\n');\n998\t        }\n999\t        combined.push_str(\"=== STDERR ===\\n\");\n1000\t        combined.push_str(stderr);\n1001\t        if !stderr.ends_with('\\n') {\n1002\t            combined.push('\\n');\n1003\t        }\n1004\t    }\n1005\t\n1006\t    combined\n1007\t}\n1008\t\n1009\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n1010\t// pub code: Option<String>,\n    /// Error variant classification.\n    pub variant: CompilationErrorVariant,\n    /// Full error message.\n    pub message: String,\n    /// File path where the error {\n    /// Create a new compilation error.\n    pub fn new(\n        code: Option<String>,\n        message: String,\n        file: Option<String>,\n        line: Option<usize>,\n        column: Option<usize>,\n    ) -> Self {\n        let variant = if let Some(ref code) = code {\n            CompilationErrorVariant::from_code(code)\n        } else {\n            CompilationErrorVariant::Syntax\n        };\n\n        CompilationError {\n            code,\n            variant,\n            message,\n            file,\n            line,\n            column,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Create a compilation error from an error line and optional location info.\n    pub fn from_error_line(line: &str) -> Self {\n        let (code, message) = Self::parse_error_code_and_message(line);\n        let variant = code\n            .as_ref()\n            .map(|c| CompilationErrorVariant::from_code(c))\n            .unwrap_or(CompilationErrorVariant::Syntax);\n\n        CompilationError {\n            code,\n            variant,\n            message,\n            file: None,\n            line: None,\n            column: None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Parse error code and message from an error line.\n    fn parse_error_code_and_message(line: &str) -> (Option<String>, String) {\n        let line = line.trim();\n\n        // Match \"error[E0308]: mismatched types\" pattern\n        if let Some(start) = line.find(\"error[\") {\n            if let Some(end) = line.find(']') {\n                let error_code = line[start + 6..end].to_string();\n                let message = if end + 1 < line.len() {\n                    let rest = line[end + 1..].trim();\n                    if rest.starts_with(':') {\n                        rest[1..].trim().to_string()\n                    } else {\n                        rest.to_string()\n                    }\n                } else {\n                    String::new()\n                };\n                return (Some(error_code), message);\n            }\n        }\n\n        // No error code found\n        (None, line.to_string())\n    }\n}\n\nimpl TestOutcome {\n    /// Returns true if cargo test exited with code 0.\n    pub fn success(&self) -> bool {\n        self.exit_code == Some(0) && !self.timed_out\n    }\n\n    /// Returns true if the failure was due to compilation errors.\n    pub fn is_compilation_failure(&self) -> bool {\n        self.compilation_failed\n    }\n\n    /// Returns true if the failure was due to test failures (not compilation).\n    pub fn is_test_failure(&self) -> bool {\n        !self.success() && !self.timed_out && !self.compilation_failed\n    }\n\n    /// Returns a human-readable summary of the outcome.\n    pub fn summary(&self) -> String {\n        if self.timed_out {\n            format!(\"Timed out after {:?}\", self.duration)\n        } else if self.compilation_failed {\n            format!(\n                \"Compilation failed with {} error(s) in {:?}\",\n                self.compilation_errors.len(),\n                self.duration\n            )\n        } else if self.success() {\n            format!(\"Passed in {:?}\", self.duration)\n        } else {\n            format!(\n                \"Failed with exit code {:?} in {:?}\",\n                self.exit_code, self.duration\n            )\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Returns a summary of compilation errors, if any.\n    pub fn compilation_error_summary(&self) -> Option<String> {\n        if self.compilation_errors.is_empty() {\n            return None;\n        }\n\n        let mut summary = format!(\"{} compilation error(s):\\n\", self.compilation_errors.len());\n\n        for (i, error) in self.compilation_errors.iter().enumerate() {\n            summary.push_str(&format!(\"  {}. \", i + 1));\n\n            // Add error code if present\n            if let Some(ref code) = error.code {\n                summary.push_str(&format!(\"[{}] \", code));\n            }\n\n            // Add variant name\n            summary.push_str(&format!(\"({})\", error.variant.name()));\n\n            // Add message (truncated if too long)\n            let message = if error.message.len() > 80 {\n                format!(\"{}...\", &error.message[..77])\n            } else {\n                error.message.clone()\n            };\n            summary.push_str(&format!(\": {}\\n\", message));\n\n            // Add file location if available\n            if let Some(ref file) = error.file {\n                summary.push_str(&format!(\"     at {}:{}\", file, error.line.unwrap_or(0)));\n                if let Some(col) = error.column {\n                    summary.push_str(&format!(\":{}\", col));\n                }\n                summary.push('\\n');\n            }\n        }\n\n        Some(summary)\n    }\n\n    /// Convert this outcome to structured metrics.\n    pub fn to_metrics(&self, test_name: String) -> TestMetrics {\n        TestMetrics {\n            test_name,\n            exit_code: self.exit_code,\n            duration_ms: self.duration.as_millis() as u64,\n            timed_out: self.timed_out,\n            stdout_len: self.stdout.len(),\n            stderr_len: self.stderr.len(),\n            timestamp: chrono::Utc::now(),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Test Metrics\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Structured test metrics for storage and analysis.\n///\n/// This type captures the essential metrics from a test run in a\n/// serializable format that can be written to disk or sent to\n/// telemetry systems.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct TestMetrics {\n    /// Name of the test that was run.\n    pub test_name: String,\n    /// Exit code from cargo test (None if killed by signal).\n    pub exit_code: Option<i32>,\n    /// Duration of the test run in milliseconds.\n    pub duration_ms: u64,\n    /// Whether the test timed out.\n    pub timed_out: bool,\n    /// Length of captured stdout in bytes.\n    pub stdout_len: usize,\n    /// Length of captured stderr in bytes.\n    pub stderr_len: usize,\n    /// When the test completed.\n    pub timestamp: chrono::DateTime<chrono::Utc>,\n}\n\nimpl TestMetrics {\n    /// Returns true if the test succeeded (exit code 0 and no timeout).\n    pub fn success(&self) -> bool {\n        self.exit_code == Some(0) && !self.timed_out\n    }\n\n    /// Get the duration as a Duration.\n    pub fn duration(&self) -> Duration {\n        Duration::from_millis(self.duration_ms)\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Compilation Error Detection\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Detect compilation errors from cargo test stderr.\n///\n/// Returns (compilation_failed, errors) where compilation_failed is true\n/// if stderr contains compilation error patterns, and errors is a list\n/// of parsed compilation errors.\npub fn detect_compilation_errors(stderr: &str) -> (bool, Vec<CompilationError>) {\n    let mut compilation_failed = false;\n    let mut errors = Vec::new();\n\n    // Cargo compilation error patterns\n    // 1. \"error[E####]: \" - Rust compiler errors with error codes\n    // 2. \"error: could not compile \" - Compilation failed message\n    // 3. \"error: aborting due to \" - Abort message\n    // 4. \"error: \" followed by a filename - General compilation errors\n\n    for line in stderr.lines() {\n        let line = line.trim();\n\n        // Check for Rust compiler error codes (e.g., \"error[E0308]:\")\n        if line.starts_with(\"error[E\") {\n            compilation_failed = true;\n            let error = CompilationError::from_error_line(line);\n            errors.push(error);\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        // Check for \"could not compile\" message\n        if line.contains(\"could not compile\") {\n            compilation_failed = true;\n            // Preserve the original error message for test verification\n            let message = line.trim().to_string();\n            errors.push(CompilationError::new(None, message, None, None, None));\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        // Check for \"aborting due to\" message\n        // Only count this if we've already seen actual compilation errors\n        if line.contains(\"aborting due to\") && compilation_failed {\n            if let Some(count) = extract_error_count(line) {\n                let message = format!(\"Aborted due to {} error(s)\", count);\n                errors.push(CompilationError::new(None, message, None, None, None));\n            }\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        // Check for general \"error:\" messages (but not warnings)\n        if line.starts_with(\"error:\") && !line.starts_with(\"error[E\") {\n            // Only capture if it looks like a compilation error, not a test error\n            if line.contains(\"unused\") || line.contains(\"dead_code\") || line.contains(\"mutability\")\n            {\n                // These are compiler warnings/lints, not test failures\n                compilation_failed = true;\n                let error = CompilationError::new(\n                    Some(\"unused\".to_string()),\n                    line.to_string(),\n                    None,\n                    None,\n                    None,\n                );\n                errors.push(error);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    (compilation_failed, errors)\n}\n\n/// Parse an error line to extract the error message.\n///\n/// Input: \"error[E0308]: mismatched types\"\n/// Output: Some(\"E0308: mismatched types\")\nfn parse_error_line(line: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    // Extract everything after \"error[\" until end of line\n    if let Some(start) = line.find(\"error[\") {\n        if let Some(end) = line.find(']') {\n            let error_code = &line[start + 6..end]; // Skip \"error[\"\n            let message = line[end + 1..].trim(); // Skip \"]\"\n                                                  // Check if message is empty or just a colon\n            if !message.is_empty() && message != \":\" {\n                return Some(format!(\"{}: {}\", error_code, message));\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    None\n}\n\n/// Extract crate name from \"could not compile\" message.\n///\n/// Input: \"error: could not compile `my_crate`\"\n/// Output: Some(\"my_crate\")\nfn extract_crate_name(line: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    if let Some(start) = line.find('`') {\n        if let Some(end) = line.rfind('`') {\n            if start < end {\n                return Some(line[start + 1..end].to_string());\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    None\n}\n\n/// Extract error count from \"aborting due to\" message.\n///\n/// Input: \"aborting due to 3 previous errors\"\n/// Output: Some(3)\nfn extract_error_count(line: &str) -> Option<usize> {\n    // Find the number in the line\n    let words: Vec<&str> = line.split_whitespace().collect();\n    for word in words {\n        if let Ok(n) = word.parse::<usize>() {\n            return Some(n);\n        }\n    }\n    None\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Cargo Test Runner\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Runner for cargo test commands.\n///\n/// ## Example\n///\n/// ```no_run\n/// use needle::cargo_test::{CargoTest, TestArgs};\n/// use std::path::Path;\n///\n/// let args = TestArgs::new()\n///     .with_target(\"--lib\")\n///     .with_filter(\"integration\");\n///\n/// let runner = CargoTest::with_args(Path::new(\"/workspace\"), args);\n/// let outcome = runner.run().unwrap();\n/// ```\npub struct CargoTest {\n    /// Workspace directory where cargo will run.\n    workspace: PathBuf,\n    /// Test arguments.\n    args: TestArgs,\n    /// Timeout in seconds.\n    timeout_secs: u64,\n}\n\nimpl CargoTest {\n    /// Create a new cargo test runner with default arguments.\n    pub fn new(workspace: &Path) -> Self {\n        CargoTest {\n            workspace: workspace.to_path_buf(),\n            args: TestArgs::default(),\n            timeout_secs: DEFAULT_TEST_TIMEOUT_SECS,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Create a new cargo test runner with custom arguments.\n    pub fn with_args(workspace: &Path, args: TestArgs) -> Self {\n        CargoTest {\n            workspace: workspace.to_path_buf(),\n            args,\n            timeout_secs: DEFAULT_TEST_TIMEOUT_SECS,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Set a custom timeout (default is 600 seconds).\n    pub fn with_timeout(mut self, timeout_secs: u64) -> Self {\n        self.timeout_secs = timeout_secs;\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// Run cargo test with the configured arguments.\n    ///\n    /// ## Errors\n    ///\n    /// Returns an error if:\n    /// - The cargo binary cannot be found\n    /// - The workspace directory is invalid\n    /// - The process cannot be spawned\n    pub fn run(&self) -> Result<TestOutcome> {\n        let start = Instant::now();\n        let args = self.args.build_args();\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            workspace = %self.workspace.display(),\n            args = ?args,\n            \"running cargo test\"\n        );\n\n        // Build the cargo command\n        let mut cmd = Command::new(\"cargo\");\n        cmd.args(&args);\n        cmd.current_dir(&self.workspace);\n        cmd.stdout(Stdio::piped());\n        cmd.stderr(Stdio::piped());\n\n        // Spawn the process with timeout handling\n        let timeout = Duration::from_secs(self.timeout_secs);\n\n        // Use a thread to handle output() with timeout\n        let output_result = std::thread::spawn(move || cmd.output());\n\n        // Wait for thread completion with timeout\n        let output = loop {\n            if start.elapsed() >= timeout {\n                return Ok(TestOutcome {\n                    exit_code: None,\n                    stdout: String::new(),\n                    stderr: String::from(\"command timed out\"),\n                    duration: start.elapsed(),\n                    timed_out: true,\n                    compilation_failed: false,\n                    compilation_errors: Vec::new(),\n                });\n            }\n\n            // Check if thread is complete\n            if output_result.is_finished() {\n                match output_result.join() {\n                    Ok(Ok(output)) => break output,\n                    Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                        return Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\"failed to execute cargo test: {}\", e))\n                            .with_context(|| \"failed to spawn or execute cargo test\");\n                    }\n                    Err(_) => {\n                        return Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\"cargo test thread panicked\"));\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n\n            std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100));\n        };\n\n        let stdout = truncate_output(&String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout));\n        let stderr = truncate_output(&String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr));\n\n        // Detect compilation errors\n        let (compilation_failed, compilation_errors) =\n            detect_compilation_errors(&String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr));\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            exit_code = ?output.status.code(),\n            duration_secs = start.elapsed().as_secs(),\n            success = output.status.success(),\n            compilation_failed,\n            compilation_error_count = compilation_errors.len(),\n            \"cargo test completed\"\n        );\n\n        Ok(TestOutcome {\n            exit_code: output.status.code(),\n            stdout,\n            stderr,\n            duration: start.elapsed(),\n            timed_out: false,\n            compilation_failed,\n            compilation_errors,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Get the workspace directory.\n    pub fn workspace(&self) -> &Path {\n        &self.workspace\n    }\n\n    /// Get the test arguments.\n    pub fn args(&self) -> &TestArgs {\n        &self.args\n    }\n\n    /// Get the timeout in seconds.\n    pub fn timeout_secs(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.timeout_secs\n    }\n\n    /// Run cargo test and write output to files.\n    ///\n    /// This method runs `cargo test` and writes the captured stdout, stderr,\n    /// and combined output to separate files in the `.test_outputs/<test_name>/` directory.\n    ///\n    /// ## Arguments\n    ///\n    /// * `test_name` - A unique identifier for the test (e.g., \"integration_test_1\")\n    ///\n    /// ## Errors\n    ///\n    /// Returns an error if:\n    /// - The test run fails\n    /// - Output directory creation fails\n    /// - File writing fails\n    ///\n    /// ## Example\n    ///\n    /// ```no_run\n    /// use needle::cargo_test::CargoTest;\n    /// use std::path::Path;\n    ///\n    /// let runner = CargoTest::new(Path::new(\"/workspace\"));\n    /// let outcome = runner.run_with_output_files(\"my_test\").unwrap();\n    /// ```\n    pub fn run_with_output_files(&self, test_name: &str) -> Result<TestOutcome> {\n        // First run the test to get the outcome\n        let outcome = self.run()?;\n\n        // Create test output directory and write outputs\n        if let Some(output) = TestOutput::new(test_name, &self.workspace) {\n            // Write stdout\n            if let Err(e) = output.write_stdout(&outcome.stdout) {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    test_name = %test_name,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to write stdout to file\"\n                );\n            }\n\n            // Write stderr\n            if let Err(e) = output.write_stderr(&outcome.stderr) {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    test_name = %test_name,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to write stderr to file\"\n                );\n            }\n\n            // Write combined output\n            let combined = create_combined_output(&outcome.stdout, &outcome.stderr);\n            if let Err(e) = output.write_combined(&combined) {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    test_name = %test_name,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to write combined output to file\"\n                );\n            }\n\n            tracing::info!(\n                test_name = %test_name,\n                stdout_path = %output.stdout_path().display(),\n                stderr_path = %output.stderr_path().display(),\n                combined_path = %output.combined_path().display(),\n                \"test output written to files\"\n            );\n        } else {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                test_name = %test_name,\n                \"failed to create test output directory, output files not written\"\n            );\n        }\n\n        Ok(outcome)\n    }\n\n    /// Run cargo test and write output to bead trace directory.\n    ///\n    /// This method runs `cargo test` and writes the captured stdout and stderr\n    /// to files in the `.beads/traces/<bead-id>/` directory. This is used to\n    /// record test execution output for debugging and analysis.\n    ///\n    /// ## Arguments\n    ///\n    /// * `bead_id` - The bead ID to use for the trace directory name\n    ///\n    /// ## Errors\n    ///\n    /// Returns an error if:\n    /// - The test run fails\n    /// - Trace directory creation fails\n    /// - File writing fails\n    ///\n    /// ## Example\n    ///\n    /// ```no_run\n    /// use needle::cargo_test::CargoTest;\n    /// use std::path::Path;\n    ///\n    /// let runner = CargoTest::new(Path::new(\"/workspace\"));\n    /// let bead_id = \"bf-12345\";\n    /// let outcome = runner.run_with_bead_trace(bead_id).unwrap();\n    /// ```\n    pub fn run_with_bead_trace(&self, bead_id: &str) -> Result<TestOutcome> {\n        // First run the test to get the outcome\n        let outcome = self.run()?;\n\n        // Create bead trace directory and write outputs\n        let bead_id = BeadId::from(bead_id);\n        if let Some(trace) = TraceCapture::new(&bead_id, &self.workspace) {\n            // Write stdout\n            if let Err(e) = trace.write_stdout(&outcome.stdout) {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead_id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to write stdout to trace file\"\n                );\n            }\n\n            // Write stderr\n            if let Err(e) = trace.write_stderr(&outcome.stderr) {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead_id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to write stderr to trace file\"\n                );\n            }\n\n            // Write test metrics (exit code, duration, etc.)\n            let test_name = format!(\"cargo_test_{}\", bead_id.as_ref());\n            let metrics = outcome.to_metrics(test_name);\n            if let Err(e) = trace.write_test_metrics(&metrics) {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead_id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to write test metrics to trace file\"\n                );\n            }\n\n            // Write compilation errors if any were detected\n            if !outcome.compilation_errors.is_empty() {\n                if let Err(e) = trace.write_compilation_errors(&outcome.compilation_errors) {\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        bead_id = %bead_id,\n                        error = %e,\n                        \"failed to write compilation errors to trace file\"\n                    );\n                }\n            }\n\n            // Write combined test output (stdout + stderr)\n            let combined = create_combined_output(&outcome.stdout, &outcome.stderr);\n            if let Err(e) = trace.write_test_output(&combined) {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead_id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to write combined test output to trace file\"\n                );\n            }\n\n            tracing::info!(\n                bead_id = %bead_id,\n                trace_dir = %trace.trace_dir().display(),\n                stdout_path = %trace.trace_dir().join(\"stdout.txt\").display(),\n                stderr_path = %trace.trace_dir().join(\"stderr.txt\").display(),\n                test_output_path = %trace.trace_dir().join(\"test-output.txt\").display(),\n                metrics_path = %trace.trace_dir().join(\"test_metrics.json\").display(),\n                compilation_errors_path = %trace.trace_dir().join(\"compilation_errors.json\").display(),\n                exit_code = ?outcome.exit_code,\n                duration_ms = outcome.duration.as_millis(),\n                compilation_error_count = outcome.compilation_errors.len(),\n                \"test output, metrics, and compilation errors written to bead trace files\"\n            );\n        } else {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                bead_id = %bead_id,\n                \"failed to create bead trace directory, output files not written\"\n            );\n        }\n\n        Ok(outcome)\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Utility Functions\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Truncate output to at most MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES.\nfn truncate_output(s: &str) -> String {\n    if s.len() <= MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES {\n        s.to_string()\n    } else {\n        let truncated = &s[..MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES];\n        format!(\"{}... [truncated]\", truncated)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Create combined output from stdout and stderr.\n///\n/// This function combines stdout and stderr into a single string with section headers.\n///\n/// ## Example\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::cargo_test::create_combined_output;\n///\n/// let stdout = \"Test output line 1\\nTest output line 2\";\n/// let stderr = \"Error message\";\n/// let combined = create_combined_output(stdout, stderr);\n/// ```\npub fn create_combined_output(stdout: &str, stderr: &str) -> String {\n    let mut combined = String::new();\n\n    if !stdout.is_empty() {\n        combined.push_str(\"=== STDOUT ===\\n\");\n        combined.push_str(stdout);\n        if !stdout.ends_with('\\n') {\n            combined.push('\\n');\n        }\n    }\n\n    if !stderr.is_empty() {\n        if !combined.is_empty() {\n            combined.push('\\n');\n        }\n        combined.push_str(\"=== STDERR ===\\n\");\n        combined.push_str(stderr);\n        if !stderr.ends_with('\\n') {\n            combined.push('\\n');\n        }\n    }\n\n    combined\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Tests\n// files were\n408\t        // already removed in a previous run but the metadata update failed\n409\t        // or was interrupted. This check is crucial for preventing infinite\n410\t        // loops where the same trace is counted repeatedly.\n411\t        let has_data_files = [\"trace.jsonl\", STDOUT_FILE, STDERR_FILE, TEST_OUTPUT_FILE]\n412\t            .iter()\n413\t            .any(|file| path.join(file).exists());\n414\t\n415\t        let should_delete = is_failed && age_days > retention_days_failed as u64;\n416\t        // Only prune if metadata says not pruned AND data files actually exist.\n417\t        // If files are gone but metadata says not pruned, we have a partial\n418\t        // state from an interrupted run - fix the metadata and skip counting.\n419\t        let should_prune =\n420\t            !is_failed && !is_pruned && has_data_files && age_days > retention_days_success as u64;\n421\t\n422\t        // Fix up metadata for traces that were partially pruned (files gone\n423\t        // but metadata not updated). This prevents infinite loops.\n424\t        if !is_failed && !is_pruned && !has_data_files && age_days > retention_days_success as u64 {\n425\t            if let Err(e) = fix_pruned_metadata(&path) {\n426\t                tracing::debug!(\n427\t                    path = %path.display(),\n428\t                    error = %e,\n429\t                    \"failed to fix pruned metadata for partially-pruned trace\"\n430\t                );\n431\t            }\n432\t        }\n433\t\n434\t        if should_delete {\n435\t            // Delete entire trace directory.\n436\t            if let Err(e) = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&path) {\n437\t                tracing::warn!(\n438\t                    path = %path.display(),\n439\t                    error = %e,\n440\t                    \"failed to delete old trace directory\"\n441\t                );\n442\t            } else {\n443\t                summary.traces_deleted += 1;\n444\t            }\n445\t        } else if should_prune {\n446\t            // Prune trace data, keep metadata.\n447\t            if let Err(e) = prune_trace_dir(&path) {\n448\t                tracing::warn!(\n449\t                    path = %path.display(),\n450\t                    error = %e,\n451\t                    \"failed to prune trace data\"\n452\t                );\n453\t            } else {\n454\t                summary.traces_pruned += 1;\n455\t            }\n456\t        }\n457\t    }\n458\t\n459\t    Ok(summary)\n460\t}\n461\t\n462\t/// Fix metadata for a trace that was partially pruned (data files gone but\n463\t/// metadata not updated). This is a recovery operation for interrupted pruning.\n464\tfn fix_pruned_metadata(trace_dir: &Path) -> Result<()> {\n465\t    let metadata_path = trace_dir.join(\"metadata.json\");\n466\t    if !metadata_path.exists() {\n467\t        return Ok(());\n468\t    }\n469\t\n470\t    let content = std::fs::read_to_string(&metadata_path)?;\n471\t    if let Ok(mut metadata) = serde_json::from_str::<TraceMetadata>(&content) {\n472\t        if !metadata.pruned {\n473\t            metadata.pruned = true;\n474\t            let json = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&metadata)?;\n475\t            std::fs::write(&metadata_path, json)?;\n476\t            tracing::debug!(\n477\t                path = %trace_dir.display(),\n478\t                \"fixed pruned metadata for partially-pruned trace\"\n479\t            );\n480\t        }\n481\t    }\n482\t    Ok(())\n483\t}\n484\t\n485\t/// Prune trace data files in a directory, keeping only metadata.json.\n486\t///\n487\t/// Updates metadata FIRST to mark as pruned, then removes data files.\n488\t/// This order is critical: if the process is interrupted after metadata\n489\t/// update but before file removal, the next cleanup will skip this trace\n490\t/// (because is_pruned=true) and only remove remaining files. This prevents\n491\t/// infinite loops where the same traces are counted as \"pruned\" repeatedly.\n492\tfn prune_trace_dir(trace_dir: &Path) -> Result<()> {\n493\t    // Step 1: Update metadata to mark as pruned BEFORE removing files.\n494\t    // This prevents the same trace from being counted as pruned multiple times\n495\t    // if the process is interrupted between metadata update and file removal.\n496\t    let metadata_path = trace_dir.join(\"metadata.json\");\n497\t    if metadata_path.exists() {\n498\t        let content = std::fs::read_to_string(&metadata_path)?;\n499\t        if let Ok(mut metadata) = serde_json::from_str::<TraceMetadata>(&content) {\n500\t            metadata.pruned = true;\n501\t            let json = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&metadata)?;\n502\t            std::fs::write(&metadata_path, json)?;\n503\t        }\n504\t    }\n505\t\n506\t    // Step 2: Remove trace data files after metadata is updated.\n507\t    // Use ? to propagate errors - if file removal fails, the operator should\n508\t    // know so they can investigate. Files that don't exist are skipped.\n509\t    for file in [\"trace.jsonl\", STDOUT_FILE, STDERR_FILE, TEST_OUTPUT_FILE] {\n510\t        let path = trace_dir.join(file);\n511\t        if path.exists() {\n512\t            std::fs::remove_file(&path)\n513\t                .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to prune trace file: {}\", path.display()))?;\n514\t        }\n515\t    }\n516\t\n517\t    Ok(())\n518\t}\n519\t\n520\tuse std::time::SystemTime;\n521\t\n522\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n523\t// Tests\n524\t// of traces pruned (metadata kept).\n    pub traces_pruned: u32,\n    /// Number of traces fully deleted.\n    pub traces_deleted: u32,\n}\n\n/// Clean up old traces based on retention policy.\n///\n/// - Failed beads (non-zero exit): delete after 30 days\n/// - Successful beads (exit 0): prune data after 7 days, keep metadata only\npub fn cleanup_traces(\n    traces_dir: &Path,\n    retention_days_failed: u32,\n    retention_days_success: u32,\n) -> Result<TraceCleanupSummary> {\n    let mut summary = TraceCleanupSummary::default();\n\n    if !traces_dir.exists() {\n        return Ok(summary);\n    }\n\n    let now = SystemTime::now()\n        .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)\n        .map(|d| d.as_secs())\n        .unwrap_or(0);\n\n    // Iterate through bead trace directories.\n    for entry in std::fs::read_dir(traces_dir)\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to read traces directory: {}\", traces_dir.display()))?\n    {\n        let entry = match entry {\n            Ok(e) => e,\n            Err(_) => continue,\n        };\n\n        let path = entry.path();\n\n        // Only process directories (bead-id subdirectories).\n        if !path.is_dir() {\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        // Check metadata.json to determine outcome and age.\n        let metadata_path = path.join(\"metadata.json\");\n        let metadata: Option<TraceMetadata> = metadata_path\n            .exists()\n            .then(|| {\n                let content = std::fs::read_to_string(&metadata_path).ok()?;\n                serde_json::from_str(&content).ok()\n            })\n            .flatten();\n\n        let age_days = metadata\n            .as_ref()\n            .and_then(|m| now.checked_sub(m.captured_at.timestamp() as u64))\n            .map(|secs| secs / 86400)\n            .unwrap_or(u64::MAX);\n\n        let is_failed = metadata.as_ref().map(|m| m.exit_code != 0).unwrap_or(false);\n        let is_pruned = metadata.as_ref().map(|m| m.pruned).unwrap_or(false);\n\n        // Check if trace data files actually exist before attempting to prune.\n        // This prevents counting a trace as \"pruned\" when the data files were\n        // already removed in a previous run but the metadata update failed\n        // or was interrupted. This check is crucial for preventing infinite\n        // loops where the same trace is counted repeatedly.\n        let has_data_files = [\"trace.jsonl\", STDOUT_FILE, STDERR_FILE, TEST_OUTPUT_FILE]\n            .iter()\n            .any(|file| path.join(file).exists());\n\n        let should_delete = is_failed && age_days > retention_days_failed as u64;\n        // Only prune if metadata says not pruned AND data files actually exist.\n        // If files are gone but metadata says not pruned, we have a partial\n        // state from an interrupted run - fix the metadata and skip counting.\n        let should_prune =\n            !is_failed && !is_pruned && has_data_files && age_days > retention_days_success as u64;\n\n        // Fix up metadata for traces that were partially pruned (files gone\n        // but metadata not updated). This prevents infinite loops.\n        if !is_failed && !is_pruned && !has_data_files && age_days > retention_days_success as u64 {\n            if let Err(e) = fix_pruned_metadata(&path) {\n                tracing::debug!(\n                    path = %path.display(),\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to fix pruned metadata for partially-pruned trace\"\n                );\n            }\n        }\n\n        if should_delete {\n            // Delete entire trace directory.\n            if let Err(e) = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&path) {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    path = %path.display(),\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to delete old trace directory\"\n                );\n            } else {\n                summary.traces_deleted += 1;\n            }\n        } else if should_prune {\n            // Prune trace data, keep metadata.\n            if let Err(e) = prune_trace_dir(&path) {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    path = %path.display(),\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to prune trace data\"\n                );\n            } else {\n                summary.traces_pruned += 1;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    Ok(summary)\n}\n\n/// Fix metadata for a trace that was partially pruned (data files gone but\n/// metadata not updated). This is a recovery operation for interrupted pruning.\nfn fix_pruned_metadata(trace_dir: &Path) -> Result<()> {\n    let metadata_path = trace_dir.join(\"metadata.json\");\n    if !metadata_path.exists() {\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n\n    let content = std::fs::read_to_string(&metadata_path)?;\n    if let Ok(mut metadata) = serde_json::from_str::<TraceMetadata>(&content) {\n        if !metadata.pruned {\n            metadata.pruned = true;\n            let json = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&metadata)?;\n            std::fs::write(&metadata_path, json)?;\n            tracing::debug!(\n                path = %trace_dir.display(),\n                \"fixed pruned metadata for partially-pruned trace\"\n            );\n        }\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Prune trace data files in a directory, keeping only metadata.json.\n///\n/// Updates metadata FIRST to mark as pruned, then removes data files.\n/// This order is critical: if the process is interrupted after metadata\n/// update but before file removal, the next cleanup will skip this trace\n/// (because is_pruned=true) and only remove remaining files. This prevents\n/// infinite loops where the same traces are counted as \"pruned\" repeatedly.\nfn prune_trace_dir(trace_dir: &Path) -> Result<()> {\n    // Step 1: Update metadata to mark as pruned BEFORE removing files.\n    // This prevents the same trace from being counted as pruned multiple times\n    // if the process is interrupted between metadata update and file removal.\n    let metadata_path = trace_dir.join(\"metadata.json\");\n    if metadata_path.exists() {\n        let content = std::fs::read_to_string(&metadata_path)?;\n        if let Ok(mut metadata) = serde_json::from_str::<TraceMetadata>(&content) {\n            metadata.pruned = true;\n            let json = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&metadata)?;\n            std::fs::write(&metadata_path, json)?;\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Step 2: Remove trace data files after metadata is updated.\n    // Use ? to propagate errors - if file removal fails, the operator should\n    // know so they can investigate. Files that don't exist are skipped.\n    for file in [\"trace.jsonl\", STDOUT_FILE, STDERR_FILE, TEST_OUTPUT_FILE] {\n        let path = trace_dir.join(file);\n        if path.exists() {\n            std::fs::remove_file(&path)\n                .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to prune trace file: {}\", path.display()))?;\n        }\n    }\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nuse std::time::SystemTime;\n\n//
